title: Closing, Credit Reporting and Charge-Off of PracticePay Patient Financing Plans
content:
**Paid off.** A PracticePay Patient Financing plan closes as paid off when its balance reaches 0.00, with the closure reason paid in full within the promotion when it is a promotional plan that met its payoff test and paid in full otherwise. A charged-off plan whose balance is recovered in full also closes as paid off.

**Overpayments.** Overpayments become a credit balance refunded within the plan's credit-balance refund business days.

**Credit reporting.** Delinquency is reported to the credit bureaus once a plan reaches the plan's delinquency-reporting days past due.

**Charge-off.** A plan is charged off once the current date is at least the charge-off days past due after the oldest unpaid due date. Days past due are counted in calendar days starting the day after the oldest unpaid due date. The oldest unpaid due date is the one the plan's record shows.

| Days past due (counted from the day after the oldest unpaid due date, 120-day threshold) | Charge-off |
|---|---|
| 119 | not yet |
| 120 | yes |

**Declines and expiries.** A declined application or an expired approval carries no fee and leaves no balance.

The reporting and charge-off thresholds and the credit-balance refund days are those in the PracticePay Patient Financing fee, refund and delinquency schedules.
